title: Best LG Dehumidifier (2026): Sonoran vs. UD501KOG5 & KOJ5
dek: LG's dehumidifier lineup has shrunk to a single model. Here's whether it's worth buying, what happened to the UD501KOG5, and where to look if 50 pints is the wrong size.
description: The best LG dehumidifier in 2026: the PuriCare Sonoran DT501BKR0 versus the discontinued UD501KOG5 and UD501KOJ5, plus manuals, parts and alternatives.
intro: If you've been searching for the **LG UD501KOG5 dehumidifier**, there's news: LG's own product pages now mark it discontinued, along with its pump-equipped twin, the UD501KOJ5. That leaves the **PuriCare Sonoran DT501BKR0** as the only LG dehumidifier sold new in the US, a 50-pint, ENERGY STAR certified unit with ThinQ app control and an unusually low published noise rating.

That's a much narrower lineup than Frigidaire, Midea or GE, which each still sell several capacities. Older LGs like the 30-pint LD301EL and the 65-pint LD651EBL disappeared years ago and now show up only used or refurbished. So the real question isn't which LG to buy — it's whether a single 50-pint model fits your space.

We compared LG's current and recently discontinued models using LG's spec sheets, ENERGY STAR listings and owner reviews, then added two non-LG alternatives for rooms that need a smaller or larger machine.
topPicksLead: The **LG PuriCare Sonoran DT501BKR0** is the best LG dehumidifier, and as of this update, the only one LG still makes.

products.name: LG PuriCare Sonoran 50-Pint Dehumidifier (DT501BKR0)
pros: About 40 dB rated noise, per LG
ENERGY STAR certified
ThinQ app with Manual, Auto, Continuous and 1-Hour Boost modes
Bucket or hose drainage
More compact than the older UD501 units
products.whyWeLoveIt: It would be the top LG even if the older models were still around. A quiet published rating, genuinely useful app scheduling and a smaller cabinet make it easy to live with in a finished basement or family room.
products.performance: LG rates it at 50 pints a day with a noise level of roughly 40 dB, which is quieter than most compressor dehumidifiers in this class. The ThinQ app lets you pick a mode and adjust drying duration remotely, and you can switch between the internal bucket and a hose. If quiet operation is your main priority, our [best quiet dehumidifier](/best/best-quiet-dehumidifier/) guide has more options.

products.name: LG PuriCare 50-Pint Dehumidifier (UD501KOG5)
pros: ENERGY STAR qualified
Rated for spaces up to roughly 2,000 sq ft
13.3-pint side bucket with a clear window
Garden-hose connection for continuous draining
cons: Warranty coverage on leftover stock may be uncertain
products.whyWeLoveIt: This was LG's mainstream dehumidifier for years and the model most owners still have. It's here for reference: if you spot one at a retailer, it's old-generation stock, not current production.
products.performance: While it was sold new, it was rated at 50 pints a day for up to about 2,000 square feet, with a 13.3-pint side-loading bucket, a removable splash guard and a minimum humidity setpoint of 30%. Owners generally described it as quiet for its class, though LG never published a decibel figure. Confirm the warranty still applies before buying any remaining unit.
products.notes: You'll sometimes see it searched as "UD501K0G5" with a zero. The correct model number uses the letter O.

products.name: LG PuriCare 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump (UD501KOJ5)
pros: Built-in condensate pump
Same 50-pint hardware as the UD501KOG5
Drains to a sink, window or drain without a bucket
cons: Discontinued, with no pump model in LG's current lineup
Only available as leftover or used stock
products.whyWeLoveIt: The KOJ5 was the version to get when there was no floor drain: identical to the KOG5 but with a pump that pushed water up and out. Its discontinuation leaves LG with no pump option at all.
products.performance: It shared the KOG5's 2,000-square-foot rating and 30% minimum setpoint while adding the pump. If a pump is non-negotiable, you're better off with a current model from another brand; our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide lists the ones still in production.

products.name: Midea Cube 20-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (MAD20S1QWT)
pros: Sized for a single bedroom or office
ENERGY STAR Most Efficient in its class
Compact cube shape
Wi-Fi app control
cons: Not an LG, so no ThinQ integration
Too small for a whole basement
products.whyWeLoveIt: LG's smallest dehumidifier is also its largest. If you're drying a bedroom, closet or small bathroom, a 50-pint machine is oversized for the job, and a 20-pint unit like the Cube does it in less space for less money.
products.performance: It's rated at 20 pints a day under the current DOE test and holds a set humidity target rather than just running a fan speed. The water tank lifts out of the base in one piece. Our [best Midea dehumidifier](/best/best-midea-dehumidifier/) guide covers the 35- and 50-pint Cube sizes, too.

products.name: Santa Fe Compact70 Dehumidifier
pros: 70 pints a day at AHAM conditions
Rated for up to about 2,200 sq ft
ENERGY STAR Most Efficient
Built-in pump for set-and-forget installs
cons: Much higher cost than any LG
Utilitarian look suits basements, not living rooms
products.whyWeLoveIt: Once a basement or crawl space needs more than 50 pints a day, LG simply has nothing to offer. The Compact70 is a professional-grade step up that runs unattended for years.
products.performance: Santa Fe rates it at 70 AHAM pints a day for up to roughly 2,200 square feet, with a built-in pump and continuous operation. It's built for the damp, cool spaces where portable units struggle. See the full lineup in our [best Santa Fe dehumidifier](/best/best-santa-fe-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. For this guide, we checked each model's status directly against LG's product pages, compared published capacity, coverage and noise figures, confirmed ENERGY STAR listings and read owner reviews for recurring issues. Because LG now sells only one size, we added the alternatives we'd recommend when 50 pints is the wrong fit, chosen from the same data on other brands.

sections.heading: What to look for in an LG dehumidifier

items.label: Confirm 50 pints is the right size
items.text: LG's only current model is sized for a large room or basement. Measure first; our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) shows what each room really needs.

items.label: Know the platforms
items.text: "UD501KO" is the older PuriCare platform; "DT501BK" is the newer Sonoran with ThinQ and the lowest published noise rating.

items.label: Read the suffix
items.text: On the older platform, a G5 suffix means no pump and J5 means a built-in pump.

items.label: Treat old models as clearance
items.text: A new-in-box UD501KOG5, LD301EL or LD651EBL is old warehouse stock. Check that a warranty still applies before you pay.

items.label: Plan your drainage
items.text: With no pump model left in LG's range, you'll need a floor drain for hose draining or a willingness to empty the bucket.

sections.heading: LG dehumidifier manuals, parts and older models

blocks.text: Plenty of LG dehumidifiers are still running in basements across the country, which means plenty of owners hunting for manuals, filters and parts.

items: **Manuals:** LG keeps owner's manuals for current and many discontinued models on its support site. Search by the full model number on the label, such as UD501KOG5 or LD651EBL.

**Filters:** LG dehumidifiers use a washable mesh filter. Rinse it every few weeks of use and let it dry completely before reinstalling. Our [replacement filter guide](/guides/dehumidifier-replacement-filter/) explains when cleaning stops being enough.

**Parts:** Buckets, filters, float switches and drain fittings for discontinued models are often still available from appliance-parts suppliers. Match the full model number, since parts vary between versions.
**Older-model recalls:** Before using a secondhand unit, especially a very old one, check its model number against CPSC.gov.
**Troubleshooting:** If an older LG runs but collects no water, work through our [dehumidifier not collecting water](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/) checklist before buying parts.

sections.heading: When an LG isn't the right fit

blocks.text: LG's single-size lineup leaves gaps on both ends. For a bedroom or office, a 20-pint unit like the **Midea Cube 20** is cheaper and smaller. For a big basement or crawl space, a 70-pint professional unit like the **Santa Fe Compact70** keeps up where any 50-pint portable would run nonstop. If you need a pump in a mainstream portable, consider current pump models from Frigidaire or GE.

blocks.title: About LG portable air conditioners
blocks.text: LG's portable ACs include a dehumidify mode, but they're built to cool and they vent warm air outside. They're no substitute for a dedicated dehumidifier in a cool, damp space. Our [dehumidifier vs. air conditioner](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-air-conditioner/) guide explains why.

The **LG PuriCare Sonoran DT501BKR0** is the best LG dehumidifier and the only one LG still sells new. It's quiet, ENERGY STAR certified and easy to control from your phone. The **UD501KOG5** and **UD501KOJ5** are discontinued, so only consider them as verified clearance stock with a valid warranty. And if your space needs fewer or more than 50 pints a day, the **Midea Cube 20** or **Santa Fe Compact70** will serve you better than forcing an LG to fit.

faqs.q: What is the best LG dehumidifier?
faqs.a: The LG PuriCare Sonoran DT501BKR0. It's rated at 50 pints a day, ENERGY STAR certified, rated at roughly 40 dB and controllable through the LG ThinQ app. It's also LG's only current dehumidifier.

faqs.q: Is the LG UD501KOG5 dehumidifier discontinued?
faqs.a: Yes. LG's product pages mark both the UD501KOG5 and the pump-equipped UD501KOJ5 as discontinued, with no official replacement named. Any unit you find for sale is leftover or used stock, so confirm the warranty before buying.
Not currently. LG's only active model is the 50-pint Sonoran. If you see a 45-pint LG listing, it's an older or secondhand model; check the full model number and status on LG's site before buying.

faqs.q: Where can I find an LG dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: On LG's support website. Search by the full model number from the unit's rating label. Manuals for many discontinued models, including the UD501 and LD series, are still posted there.

faqs.q: Can I still get parts for an older LG dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Common parts like buckets, filters, float switches and drain fittings are sold by appliance-parts suppliers. Match the complete model number, and if a sealed-system part like the compressor fails on an old unit, replacement is usually more sensible than repair.

faqs.q: How loud is an LG dehumidifier?
faqs.a: LG rates the Sonoran DT501BKR0 at about 40 dB, which is quiet for a 50-pint compressor unit. The discontinued UD501KOG5 and UD501KOJ5 had no published decibel rating, but owners generally described them as quiet for their size.

faqs.q: What if I need a smaller or larger LG dehumidifier?
faqs.a: LG doesn't make one right now. For a small room, a 20-pint unit like the Midea Cube 20 is a better fit. For a large basement or crawl space, a 70-pint professional unit like the Santa Fe Compact70 covers more ground than any current LG.
